title: Chapter 19 — Pro-Style Ranges & Luxury Cooking
intro: The pro-style range universe — Wolf, Thermador, Viking, BlueStar, Bertazzoni and the conversation that sells them.

sections.title: The Pro-Style Landscape
sections.content:
Pro-style ranges are lifestyle purchases. The customer buying a $5,000-$15,000 range is not just cooking dinner — they are making a statement about their kitchen, their home, and their identity as a cook.

The major players: Wolf is the benchmark — built in Madison, Wisconsin, infrared broiler, dual-stacked burners, and the strongest brand recognition in luxury cooking. Thermador brings the Star Burner and the One-Two-Free rebate program — buy qualifying appliances and get a free dishwasher. Viking was the original pro-style pioneer but has had reliability perception challenges. BlueStar offers the highest BTU output in the residential market and fully customizable colours. Bertazzoni brings Italian design heritage and a more approachable price point for the pro-style aesthetic.

Know each brand's story. At this level, the story sells as much as the spec.

sections.title: The Installation Reality
sections.content:
Pro-style ranges have serious installation requirements that must be verified before the sale. Gas line capacity: a 48-inch pro range may need a 3/4-inch gas line, not the 1/2-inch standard residential line. Ventilation: CFM must match BTU output — 1 CFM per 100 BTU minimum. A 60,000 BTU range needs 600 CFM minimum ventilation. Ductwork path and exterior termination must exist.

Electrical: even gas ranges need 120V for ignition and controls. Some dual-fuel models need 240V for the electric oven. Anti-tip bracket is code-required.

Weight: a 48-inch pro range can weigh 400-600 pounds. Verify the floor can support it. Verify the delivery path can accommodate it. These are not details to discover on delivery day.

sections.title: Selling the Experience
sections.content:
Do not sell pro-style ranges on specs. Sell them on the cooking experience. 'Wolf ranges are built in a single factory in Wisconsin. Each range takes about three hours to assemble by hand. The infrared broiler is exclusive to Wolf — it reaches 1,800 degrees and sears like a restaurant broiler.'

The demo matters enormously at this tier. Turn on the burners. Show the flame response. Open the oven door and let them feel the build quality. Let them grip the handles. Pro-style ranges are tactile — the weight, the knobs, the grates — and the demo lets the customer feel the investment.

Involve Leah for design context and Asher for installation requirements. The customer at this tier expects a team, not a solo rep.
